paper.title: Nonstochastic Bandits with Infinitely Many Experts

settings.name_in_paper: Nonstochastic bandits with a finite number of experts
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t \in [T]$, the adversary first sets a reward vector $r(t) \in [0,1]^K$ ... Each expert $i$ then gives their advice $\xi^i(t)$, which is a probability vector over $\A$. ... the learner receives the reward $r_{a(t)}(t)$ and no other information. We start with a simplified problem where the number of experts is finite.

settings.name_in_paper: Nonstochastic bandits with infinitely many experts
unmapped: countably infinite set of indexed experts; learner may query only a finite subset of experts' advice each round
regret is measured against the globally best expert i*, whose index is unknown
settings.definition_quote: Each expert $i \in \Z$ then gives their advice $\xi^i(t)$ ... After querying a finite subset of the experts' advice but not the rewards, the learner then samples an action $a(t)$. ... The learner's goal is to minimize $\text{Regret}(T)$, the regret with respect to the globally best expert $i^*$.

algorithms.name: BEES.LB (BEES with Lower Bound, using PTS)

conditions: there exists a uniform expert in the expert set (advice 1/K for all actions)

source.label: propn:exp4r_ranking
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:regime_uniform_expert}, for any $\delta \in (0, 1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Exp4.R configured with $\pmin = \sqrt{\ln{N}/(KT)}$ satisfies that (i) $\text{Regret}(T; \I) \leq 7 \sqrt{KT\ln{(2N/\delta)}}$; (ii) for all $i, i' \in \I$, if $\ln w_i(T+1) - \ln w_{i'}(T+1) > \epsilon_i$, then $R_i(T) > R_{i'}(T)$.

results.notes: Regret is vs expected total reward of best expert minus realized reward. Lemma 2 gives the same bound conditional on event E(delta); combined here. Part (ii) is a ranking guarantee, not recorded separately.

symbols.alpha_ep: BEES growth exponent alpha (positive integer): N_l = c 2^{alpha l}
symbols.c_ep: BEES constant c (positive integer) scaling number of experts per epoch
symbols.C_ep: BEES constant C(alpha,c,K,delta): epoch length T_l = C 2^l
symbols.i_star: index of the globally best expert

conditions: a uniform expert is available in each epoch
tuning: C chosen so that 4K ln(c 2^{alpha l}) <= C 2^l and ln(c 2^{alpha l+1}/delta) <= (e-2) C K 2^l for all l, e.g. C = ceil(alpha K ln(16 c^4/delta))
Exp4.R run with confidence delta/L in each epoch

source.label: thm:master_algo_pac_regret_general
source.quote: If a uniform expert is available in each epoch, then there exist absolute constants $\alpha \in \Z$ and $c \in \Z$ such that, for some $C(\alpha, c, K, \delta) \in \Z$, BEES satisfies that, for any $\delta \in (0, 1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $\text{Regret}(T) < 20\sqrt{\alpha K(T+2C) \ln (cL(2+T/C)/\delta) } + 2C ( i^*/c )^{1/\alpha}$.

results.notes: Proof shows it holds for any integers alpha, c with suitable C. Space O(K(1+T/K)^alpha), time ~K^2(1+T/K)^{alpha+1}.

symbols.i_star: index of the globally best expert

conditions: a uniform expert is available in each epoch

source.label: cor:master_algo_pac_regret_general
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:master_algo_pac_regret_general}, running BEES with $\alpha \in \Z$, $c \in \Z$, and $C=\ceil{\alpha K\ln (16c^4/\delta)}$ satisfies that, for any $\delta \in (0, 1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\text{Regret}(T) = \tbo{(i^*)^{1/\alpha}K + \sqrt{\alpha KT}}$.

results.notes: Optimal up to polylogs when i* = O~(sqrt(T/K)) with alpha=1.

symbols.C_ep: BEES constant C(alpha,c,K,delta): epoch length T_l = C 2^l
symbols.i_star: index of the globally best expert

conditions: Assumption 2: in every epoch, expected total reward is weakly unimodal in expert index, and the index of the best expert is nondecreasing over epochs
a uniform expert is available in each epoch
tuning: C = ceil(alpha K ln(16 c^4/delta)) suffices
Exp4.R run with confidence delta/L in each epoch

source.label: thm:master_algo_pac_regret_improved
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{aspn:time_variant_model_ranking}, if a uniform expert is available in each epoch, then there exist absolute constants $\alpha \in \Z$ and $c \in \Z$ such that, for some $C(\alpha, c, K, \delta) \in \Z$, BEES.LB satisfies that, for any $\delta \in (0, 1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $\text{Regret}(T) < 20\sqrt{\alpha K(T+2C) \ln (cL(2+T/C)/\delta) } + 2C ( i^*/c )^{1/\alpha}$.

results.notes: Same bound as Theorem 1; structured (unimodal) experts assumption put in conditions.
